Title: A Poincaré lemma for real-valued differential forms on Berkovich spaces
Authors: Philipp Jell
Date: Tue Sep  2 11:59:24 2014

Real-valued differential forms on Berkovich analytic spaces were introduced by Chambert-Loir and Ducros in 'Formes diff\'erentielles r\'eelles et courants sur les espaces de Berkovich' using superforms on polyhedral complexes. We prove a Poincar\'e lemma for these superforms and use it to also prove a Poincar\'e lemma for real-valued differential forms on Berkovich spaces. For superforms we further show finite dimensionality for the associated de Rham cohomology on polyhedral complexes in all (bi-)degrees. We also show finite dimensionality for the real-valued de Rham cohomology of the analytification of an algebraic variety in some bidegrees.

L46@P4: Differential forms are a fundamental tool in differential and complex geometry. For a
L47@P4: smooth manifold X the de Rham complex (A•, d) of smooth differential forms carries a
L48@P4: lot of information about the geometry of the space X. The Poincar´e lemma shows that
L49@P4: the de Rham complex is an exact complex of sheaves. It is a fundamental result of de
L50@P4: Rham from the 1930s that the cohomology of the complex of global sections (A•(X), d)
L51@P4: agrees with the singular cohomology of X with real coefficients. This in particular
L52@P4: shows that the cohomology of this complex is an invariant of the topological space X,
L53@P4: independent of the differentiable structure.

L64@P4: We now want to work over a non-archimedean field and use analytic spaces in
L65@P4: the sense of Berkovich [Ber90] instead of complex manifolds. In their fundamental
L66@P4: preprint [CLD12] Chambert–Loir and Ducros introduced real-valued differential forms
L67@P4: on Berkovich analytic spaces. Their idea is to map subsets of the analytic space into
L68@P4: analytic tori and then formally pull back superforms, as defined by Lagerberg [Lag12],
L69@P4: along tropicalization maps. They obtain a sheaf of bigraded bidifferential algebras
L70@P4: (A•,•, d0, d00) on the analytic space. They show that analogous statements of fundamental properties from complex pluri-potential theory hold for these forms. For example
L71@P4: they prove analogues of the Poincar´e–Lelong-formula and establish a variant of the
L72@P4: Bedford–Taylor approach to define products of (1, 1)-currents which satisfy suitable
L73@P4: positivity conditions.
L74@P4: Another aspect of differential forms on complex manifolds is their use in Arakelov
L75@P4: theory to calculate intersection numbers at infinite places. Gubler and K¨unnemann
L76@P4: have used an extended class of differential forms (so called δ-forms) to give an analytic
L77@P4: description of local heights also at finite places.
